claim: 1. A machine-to-machine (M2M) based wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU), comprising: a receiver configured to receive information from a M2M controller; and a subscriber identity module (SIM) card, wherein the SIM card includes a group international mobile subscriber identity (G-IMSI) wherein the G-IMSI is unique to a group of M2M WTRUs.
gold_explanation: As to claim 1, Luft discloses substantially the invention as claimed, including a machine-to-machine (M2M) based wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) (Figure 4, a M2M clients 406), comprising: a receiver configured to receive information from a M2M controller (Figure 4, the Central Maintenance Station 402; the network management entity/network operator); and a subscriber identity module (SIM) card, wherein the SIM card includes a group international mobile subscriber identity (G-IMSI) (a unique identifier, sharing the same IMSI) wherein the G-IMSI is unique to a group of M2M WTRUs ([0013]-0015]; [0047]-[0052]) (Figures 4-7 and associated text).
examiner_text: As to claim 1, Luft discloses substantially the invention as claimed, including a machine-to-machine (M2M) based wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) (Figure 4, a M2M clients 406), comprising: a receiver configured to receive information from a M2M controller (Figure 4, the Central Maintenance Station 402; the network management entity/network operator); and a subscriber identity module (SIM) card, wherein the SIM card includes a group international mobile subscriber identity (G-IMSI) (a unique identifier, sharing the same IMSI) wherein the G-IMSI is unique to a group of M2M WTRUs ([0013]-0015]; [0047]-[0052]) (Figures 4-7 and associated text).

model.explanation: The claim defines a machine-to-machine (M2M) based wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) comprising a receiver configured to receive information from a M2M controller, a subscriber identity module (SIM) card, and the SIM card includes a group international mobile subscriber identity (G-IMSI) unique to a group of M2M WTRUs. The prior art does not disclose a G-IMSI unique to a group of M2M WTRUs. The prior art discloses IMSI and MSISDN, but not a G-IMSI unique to a group of M2M WTRUs. Therefore, the claim is not rejected under 102 or 103.

claim: 18. The system of claim 15, where the response logic is further operable to: transmit a sequence of the continuation frames until the primary data is ready.
parents: 15. A system for managing a reverse direction communication channel from a responder to an initiator, the system comprising: a receiver that detects a reverse direction grant indicator sent by the initiator to the responder; a memory that stores the reverse direction grant indicator after it is received; a processor that executes response logic, the response logic operable to: determine whether the responder has primary data that is tracked by sequence control information to return to the initiator; determine whether the responder is ready with the primary data; when the primary data is not ready: prepare a continuation frame comprising a continuation indicator; and set the continuation indicator to indicate that the reverse direction communication channel from the responder to the initiator should persist; and when the primary data is ready: prepare a primary data frame comprising at least a portion of the primary data; and a transmitter that transmits the continuation frame and the primary data frame from the responder to the initiator.
gold_explanation:
In claim 18, line 2, ---the continuation frames---, has no antecedent basis.

As per claim 18, The system of claim 15, where the response logic is further operable to: transmit a sequence of the continuation frames until the primary data is ready. Cordeiro discloses, (para. 0018 lines 1-13, “ In an example, in order to respond within a SIFS, the display device 102 can continually respond by sending null frames to the video source 104. Once the display device 102 responds within SIFS, the display device 102 has continual access to the medium until the display device 102 indicates that it is done, until the TXOP/SP granted to the video source 102 ends, or until a SIFS time period passes from the last frame. The display device 102 can indicate that it is done by setting the RDG/more PPDU field to zero in a MPDU sent to the video source 104. Accordingly, as long as the display device 102 continually sends the null frames the display device 102 can maintain access to the medium until the RTT response is ready and can be sent”).
examiner_text:
In claim 18, line 2, ---the continuation frames---, has no antecedent basis.

As per claim 18, The system of claim 15, where the response logic is further operable to: transmit a sequence of the continuation frames until the primary data is ready.
